blocks.text: Stormwater Management Plan for Johnson PLC

items: Client: {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}}, a private development on a county-seat site.
Prepared by Brackenridge Civil Group, under the seal of the Principal Engineer.
Owner's contact: David Dyer, General Manager, for site information and approvals.
Work begins {{fact:f:E-2004-001.start}}, running about five months end to end.

blocks.text: What we are here to do

items: Deliver a stormwater management plan the site can actually be built from.
Meet the regional water authority's standards and clear its review on the first pass.
Control the rate and quality of runoff so the development does not burden its neighbors.
Keep the design straightforward, so it holds up under a careful reviewer's read.
Start from the survey and the drainage areas it defines, and confirm them before we model.
Model the runoff, then size detention to the release rates the authority requires.
Add the water quality treatment at the basin outlet and the erosion and sediment control plan.
Assemble the plan set and the supporting calculations for submission and review.
Pamela Warren, Project Engineer: drainage design, detention, and water authority coordination.
Charles Olson, Design Technician: base sheet, existing conditions, and drainage areas.
Jeffrey Perez, Design Technician: utility and stormwater drafting, checked to the design memoranda.
David Dyer is our single point of contact for site information and owner decisions.
We will bring our questions to you in one place, not piecemeal through the week.
We will keep you current with short progress notes as the design takes shape.
You will see the plan at a design review before we finalize any of it.
Confirm the survey and the drainage areas on the base sheet.
Build the drainage model and review the preliminary runoff figures.
Size the detention and set the water quality treatment at the basin outlet.
Meet to walk the preliminary detention design together before we commit to it.
